theodosius_canon: This is a fair primary for the facts leg of Widely Accepted, and the quotes show it. At Assemani BO III.2, lines 34466-34485, Trigault quotes the Summa canonum synodalium (II.6.19, 'decimo nono' in the OCR as 'decimo tiono') under the heading 'Canon Theodosii Patriarchae in haec verba'. The canon names six sees that attend the patriarch every fourth year. It then says that 'reliqui Metropolitae Chinae, Indiae, Persidis ... qui longissime absunt' must send 'literas consensionis (id est, communionis)' to the patriarch 'semel sexto quoque anno'. That is a metropolitan of India under the patriarch in the 850s. The note's 'write to him every six years' renders that fairly. This differs from Herberstein in kind. The text claims to give the canon 'in haec verba', not to retell events, and a canon kept in Abdisho's collection is how East Syriac synodal law survives. The chain also passes through a Latin translation (Trigault, quoted by Assemani), which is why it is right that it carries only Widely Accepted, not Documented. Mingana 1694-1696 independently has Theodosius naming 'the Archbishops of Samarkand, India, and China'. One small point: Mingana's OCR gives his years as 'A.D. 832-858' (probably 852), while the work field says 853-858. The note says only 'in the 850s', which both support, so this is not a finding.

new_findings.issue: The note says 'a church council at Uppsala backed him in 1530'. Anjou says only 'the council, which, in 1530, sat at Upsala'. Elsewhere he shows that this same council of Uppsala in 1530 resolved to take the second-largest bell of every church to pay the foreign debt. That is a meeting of the realm, not a church council. The word 'church' is not in the source.

new_findings.issue: The recast sentence 'his compromise on the will of Christ failed against the stand of Maximus the Confessor' makes Maximus the cause of the compromise's failure. The old summary listed them side by side ('the monothelete compromise and its collapse, Maximus the Confessor's resistance'), and the revision says it added no fact. The compromise was given up at the council of 680-681, years after Maximus's death. His resistance mattered, but 'failed against' says more than the old text did.

new_findings.issue: R1-02 asked that the Herberstein rule be recorded in the README. The revision states the rule: 'a sixteenth- or seventeenth-century retelling (Herberstein 1549, Kyiv Synopsis 1674) is not a primary for ninth- or tenth-century events'. It now decides six links: the two Kievan ones, the two Macedonian ones, and the two Indian ones, where it excluded the post-1580 Malabar chronicle.
